_comment: TRUE cross-mechanism polypharmacology experiment: one target per MOA class (7 classes, 7 targets), so a candidate that scores well here would have to hit genuinely different binding sites/pharmacophores at once -- not just multiple variants of the same mechanism. This is intentionally the hard version: with a simple atom-mutation GA starting from 4-12 seeds, expect 'min' aggregation to converge on a mediocre-everywhere compromise rather than a strong hit, since AChE/nAChR/GABA/ecdysone/ryanodine/Ca-channel/complex-I pharmacophores don't share structural features. Worth reporting as an exploratory result either way -- see the same-MOA-class alternative (all-AChE or all-nAChR targets) if you want a run more likely to actually converge.
_targets_comment: One target per MOA class: CHEMBL4078=acetylcholinesterase, CHEMBL2111384=nicotinic AChR, CHEMBL5445=GABA receptor/transporter, CHEMBL6045=ryanodine receptor, CHEMBL614865=mitochondrial complex I, CHEMBL3868=ecdysone receptor, CHEMBL3762=voltage-dependent Ca channel.
_aggregation_comment: 'min' rewards candidates good against ALL targets (worst-case); 'mean' rewards good-on-average candidates; 'weighted' needs target_weights below.
_seed_smiles_comment: Fallback only, used if use_real_seeds finds nothing for these targets.
